newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK mortgages slow in line with properties - Hang Sen.
newsitem.headline: HK mortgages slow in line with properties - Hang Sen.

text.p: Hang Seng Bank Ltd said on Tuesday the mortgage business had slowed in line with falling activity in the underlying property market.

"Oh yes, definitely," Vice Chairman and Chief Executive Alex Au said when asked if the mortgage business had slowed down. "I think it would be slowing down at the same rate as the slowdown in the property market."
Au said he had no figures, but he noted that new applications were slowing, while drawdowns were likely not to slow until May due to the time-lag effect.
"I think it's a very healthy phenomenon for the property market to have this...consolidation," he added.
Property transactions have been slowing and prices falling in recent months since the government introduced measures to speed the flow of supply to the market and interest rates rose.
Property deals in March fell five percent in number and nearly 12 percent in value from February. Analysts also say flat prices have eroded about 10 percent since early March.
